mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in the federal funds rate signals easier monetary policy, boosting equity markets.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS drops but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment suggests a strong labor market, which is positive for the S&P 500.
failure_condition: If unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production indicates strong economic output, positively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased demand, which should boost S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts exceed 1.5 million but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI exceeds 3%, it may indicate inflationary pressures that could negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 300 but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment increases significantly, it signals economic strength, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If payroll employment exceeds 150,000 but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales increase, it indicates strong consumer demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If retail sales exceed $700 billion but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.
